title: Deployment fidget log + threshold hypotheses
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal fidget log for small, iterative changes to rollout thresholds and safety signals. Not a canonical runbook — think of it as the desk-notes I jot during live canaries and follow-ups. The goal: make low-risk, measurable micro-adjustments so we can learn what nudges are meaningful and what just adds noise.

Context and motivation:
- Recent flakiness on small-context chat prompts (seq len ~64) after 2 model variant updates. Surface-level: latency jitter + small increase in bad-token-rate on a subset of tenants.
- Previous canaries used coarse thresholds (p50/p95 latency, error_rate > 0.5%). Too blunt. We need micro-banding and occupancy-sensitive thresholds.

Hypotheses (short):
1) A 10ms bump in p50 for tenant cohorts with high prefix-cache-hit (>= 80%) is noisy and recoverable; should not trigger full rollback.
2) Correlated rises in tail-latency + per-session hallucination signals indicate model regression needing pin/unwind.
3) Small increases in client-side timeout increments (from 5s->6s) mask true SLO violations; prefer server-side sentinel gating.

Quick glossary (my shorthand):
- BWM: background work multiplier (internal metric)
- bad-token-rate: fraction of tokens flagged by eval prompts as incorrect/unexpected (our canary probe set)
- loss-drift: smoothed delta of scoring loss on probe set vs baseline (7d EWMA)
- occupancy: GPU queue occupancy per shard

Signal design (proposed micro-bands):
- Latency p50 bands: 
  - green: <120ms (no-op)
  - amber: 120-150ms (monitor + increase sampling of probing tenants by +5x)
  - red: >150ms for >5min AND p95 >400ms -> immediate traffic throttle to 30%
- Bad-token-rate (probe set):
  - green: <0.25%
  - amber: 0.25-0.6% -> flag, require correlated metric to escalate
  - red: >0.6% -> rollback candidate if sustained 3+ windows of 2min
- Correlation rule: treat latency amber + bad-token amber AND source-tenants>5 as red-warn for manual review

Sampling and cohorting:
- Start canary with 0.5% global traffic distributed across 12 micro-cohorts (geo + SDK version + tenant-size stratified).
- After 10m steady-state: add 1% more (total 1.5%). Continue +1% every 15m if no amber signals. Stop ramp on any amber and hold for 30m.
- Shadow run for high-sensitivity tenants (finance, legal) for 24h before moving to active path.

Priming & pinning heuristics (notes to self):
- If we detect model-variant drift in the first 20 minutes but only in one geo, avoid cross-geo unpin; instead, apply region-specific pin for that cohort and run extended shadow.
- Pin template: {tenant -> pinned_model_version -> reason_tag -> ticket_id} keep minimal, prefer auto-expire after 48h unless escalated.
  (TODO: script to auto-create pinned entries with TTL)

Action ladder (what I do when things wobble):
1) amber latency only: increase probe sampling, enable extra traces for 10m, notify on-call (SRE) with short summary.
2) amber bad-token only: double probe run frequency, snapshot KV cache metrics, check quantization path metric.
3) amber both: pause ramp, cap to previous % for 30m, escalate to eng on-call + product-owner.
4) red any: throttle to 30% and initiate rollback plan (see checklist).

Rollback checklist (quick):
- Notify channels: #prod-canaries, #eng-oncall, +pager. Include canary_id, start_ts, cohorts affected, immediate actions taken.
- Switch routing to prior stable variant (model:vX.Y.Z) via runtime toggle with TTL=10m.
- Increase sampling of error traces and save full session logs for 1h.
- Create postmortem stub ticket (owner self) within 1 working day.

Observability queries (copy/paste friendly):
- Probe bad-token-rate: SELECT count_if(flagged_token)/count(*) FROM probe_tokens WHERE model_variant='CANARY' AND window=2m;
- Session tail-latency: percentile_latency(session_id, [50,95,99]) BY model_variant, region;
- Cache-hit vs latency: join(cache_hit_ratio, p95_latency) group by shard_id, model_variant

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Q1: Is our bad-token probe set sensitive to small prompt shifts? Run A/B of probe set variants with controlled paraphrases (today).
- Q2: Occupancy-aware thresholds: can we auto-lower batch sizes for cohorts hitting occupancy>0.85 to avoid tail spikes? (need infra change; spike test in staging).
- Q3: Should we bias canary sampling away from SDK versions with experimental client retries? (I think yes; retries hide server problems)

Operational notes (real-world edge cases I've hit):
- If client-side timeouts increase during canary, we see lower error rates but unchanged server latency — this masks regressions. Always cross-check client SDK versions in cohort.
- Rolling back too fast removes signal needed to debug root cause. Prefer staged pin/unpin and extended shadow for 1-2 hours when safe.

Simple timeline template (use when running live):
- T0: deploy canary traffic config + create canary_id
- T0+5m: sanity checks (health endpoints, infra drains)
- T0+10m: check green band metrics on probe set
- T0+25m: increase to target % (by +1% increments)
- Hold windows: 15m between increments; abort on amber/red

Notes-to-self (private):
- Keep noise floor metrics: #unique tenants with >1 amber signal in last 24h; if >3, probably infra noise not model.
- Add a tiny heartbeat probe (single short prompt) at T0 to detect immediate tokenization issues.

End-of-session checklist (after any canary run):
- Save timeline + traces as artifact linked in ticket.
- Record any manual interventions and reasons.
- If pinned, note TTL and owner; if unpinned, add brief rationale.

Bottom line: small adjustments (fidgets) with tight observability are better than blunt rollbacks. But we must keep two guardrails: (1) no partial-silence — signals must be easily explainable and (2) prefer region/cohort-level pins before global flips.

Random todo (dev): write a small script that accepts a list of cohorts and auto-applies a pinned model with TTL and auto-comment (link PR). Also a quick dashboard tile showing "canary fidget score" (combination of bad-token, p95 latency, occupancy) so I don't have to cross-check three panels.

-- Lin
Notes: leaving this as a living doc. Will clean and formalize if we decide to bake into runbook.
